package_info.package_manager: N/A (Delivered via email/SharePoint, not a software package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire attack chain leverages trusted Microsoft SharePoint infrastructure to host and deliver malicious PDFs containing phishing links, which ultimately lead to credential theft via fake Microsoft login pages. The campaign is designed to evade detection by using legitimate services, CAPTCHAs, and redirection logic.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: [Email body with embedded link to SharePoint-hosted PDF]
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user clicks the link in the phishing email, they are redirected to a SharePoint-hosted PDF, initiating the phishing chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unexpected emails with links to file shares are a common phishing vector, especially when the sender is unknown or the context is suspicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate file sharing emails should come from known contacts and match expected business processes.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate business file sharing via SharePoint or OneDrive.
key_indicators: Urgency or pressure tactics in email

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: [PDF with embedded link to external phishing site]
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user opens the PDF and clicks the embedded link, they are redirected to an external phishing site, often after passing through a CAPTCHA.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: PDFs hosted on trusted platforms containing links to external, unrelated domains are a strong phishing indicator.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate PDFs should not contain links to credential harvesting sites.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: PDFs with links to legitimate business resources.
key_indicators: PDF hosted on SharePoint with external link

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon visiting the phishing site, the user is presented with a CAPTCHA challenge, which must be solved before proceeding to the credential harvesting page.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: CAPTCHAs are used to evade automated analysis and make the phishing site appear more legitimate.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate CAPTCHAs are rarely used before login pages for Microsoft services.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: CAPTCHAs on high-value or sensitive login portals.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: [HTML/JavaScript code mimicking Microsoft login, capturing credentials]
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The user is presented with a fake Microsoft login page. When credentials are entered, they are sent to the attacker's server, enabling credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fake login pages designed to steal credentials are a classic phishing tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Microsoft login pages are hosted on official Microsoft domains and use proper security certificates.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; credential harvesting is always malicious.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: [JavaScript code that checks IP/ASN and redirects to legitimate site if detected as hosting provider]
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: If the phishing kit detects that the visitor is from a known hosting provider (e.g., security sandbox), it redirects them to a legitimate website to evade detection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Conditional redirection to evade sandboxes is a strong indicator of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate sites do not selectively redirect based on visitor IP/ASN.
key_indicators: Redirection to legitimate site when suspicious traffic is detected

attack_chain.action: Victim receives phishing email with link to SharePoint-hosted PDF.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim clicks link and opens PDF.

attack_chain.action: Victim opens PDF on SharePoint, which contains a link to an external phishing site.
Victim is presented with a CAPTCHA challenge on the phishing site.
Victim is shown a fake Microsoft login page and enters credentials.
If the phishing kit detects traffic from a hosting provider, it redirects to a legitimate site to evade detection.

behavioral_signatures: SharePoint-hosted PDFs containing links to external, non-Microsoft domains
Phishing sites presenting CAPTCHAs before login forms
Fake Microsoft login pages on non-Microsoft domains
Conditional redirection based on visitor IP/ASN
file_indicators: Unexpected PDF files shared via SharePoint
PDFs with embedded links to unrelated domains
network_indicators: SharePoint URLs followed by immediate navigation to non-Microsoft domains
Credential POST requests to attacker-controlled endpoints
Redirection to legitimate sites when accessed from known hosting providers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for emails containing SharePoint links that, when followed, lead to PDFs with embedded links to external domains. Flag any SharePoint-hosted PDFs that contain links to non-Microsoft or suspicious domains. Detect CAPTCHAs and login forms on non-Microsoft domains that visually mimic Microsoft branding. Analyze network traffic for credential POSTs to unknown endpoints and for redirection logic based on IP/ASN. Use sandboxing to observe full attack chain, but be aware of evasion via redirection.
